He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown Hoyas]]. In the [[2009 NBA draft]], he was drafted 35th overall by the [[Detroit Pistons]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/draft2009/ |title=NBA.com: DRAFT 2009 |work=NBA.com |access-date=September 22, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120125043428/http://www.nba.com/draft2009/ |archive-date=January 25, 2012 |url-status=dead }} ==High school career== Summers attended the [[McDonogh School]], a private school in [[Owings Mills, Maryland]]. As a junior in 2004–05, he averaged 20.4 points and 11.6 rebounds per game, helping McDonogh to a 23–6 record and to the MIAA A Conference final and a No. 5 ranking in the Baltimore Sun's final poll.{{cite web |url=http://www.guhoyas.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/summers_dajuan00.html |title=DaJuan Summers Bio |work=GUHoyas.com |access-date=September 22, 2015 |archive-date=March 3, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303232101/http://www.guhoyas.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/summers_dajuan00.html |url-status=dead }} As a senior in 2005–06, he averaged 29.2 points, 11.0 rebounds, 4.0 assists, 2.0 steals and 3.0 blocks per game, leading McDonogh to a 19–6 overall record. He finished his high school career with 1,502 points and a two-time Baltimore Sun Baltimore County Player of the Year (junior and senior). Considered a five-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Summers was listed as the No. 9 small forward and the No. 23 player in the nation in 2006.{{cite web |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-DaJuan-Summers-29824 |title=DaJuan Summers Recruiting Profile |work=Rivals.com |access-date=September 22, 2015}} ==College career== [[File:DaJuan Summers in 2006.jpg|thumb|left|upright|Summers at Georgetown.]] In his freshman season at [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown]], Summers was named to the 2007 Big East All-Rookie team. In 37 games, he averaged 9.2 points, 3.7 rebounds and 1.1 assists per game. In his sophomore season, he was a second team All-District 4 selection by the National Association of Basketball Coaches. In 33 games, he averaged 11.1 points, 5.4 rebounds and 1.5 assists per game. In his junior season, he played 31 games, averaging 13.6 points, 4.1 rebounds, 1.3 assists and 1.1 steals per game.{{cite Sports-Reference |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/dajuan-summers-1.html |title=DaJuan Summers |access-date=September 22, 2015}} On March 30, 2009, he declared for the NBA draft, foregoing his final year of college eligibility.{{cite web |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/147767-dajuan-summers-declares-for-nba-draft |title=DaJuan Summers Declares for NBA Draft |work=BleacherReport.com |date=March 30, 2009 |access-date=September 22, 2015}} ==Professional career== On June 25, 2009, Summers was selected with the 35th overall pick in the [[2009 NBA draft]] by the [[Detroit Pistons]]. In July 2009, he joined the Pistons for the 2009 NBA Summer League. In August 2009, he signed a multi-year deal with the Pistons.{{cite web |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/usa/nba/78673/detroit-pistons-sign-2009-draft-picks-dajuan-summers-and-jonas-jerebko.html |title=Detroit Pistons sign 2009 draft picks DaJuan Summers and Jonas Jerebko |work=Sportando.com |date=August 7, 2009 |access-date=September 22, 2015}} In July 2010, he re-joined the Pistons for the 2010 NBA Summer League. On July 3, 2011, he signed a two-year deal with [[Montepaschi Siena]] of Italy.{{cite web |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/87035/montepaschi-announces-former-pistons-dajuan-summers.html |title=Montepaschi announces former Pistons DaJuan Summers |work=Sportando.com |date=July 3, 2011 |access-date=September 22, 2015}} On October 30, 2011, he parted ways with Siena after just four games.{{cite web |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/88804/montepaschi-siena-and-dajuan-summers-part-ways.html |title=Montepaschi Siena and DaJuan Summers part ways |work=Sportando.com |date=October 30, 2011 |access-date=September 22, 2015}} On December 9, 2011, he signed with the [[New Orleans Pelicans|New Orleans Hornets]].{{cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=8737 |title=Hornets add nine players to training camp |work=HoopsHype.com |date=December 9, 2011 |access-date=September 22, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150314231713/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=8737 |archive-date=March 14, 2015 |url-status=dead }} On February 7, 2012, he was waived by the Hornets.{{cite web |url=http://www.nola.com/hornets/index.ssf/2012/02/new_orleans_hornets_waive_g_sq.html |title=New Orleans Hornets waive G Squeaky Johnson, G/F DaJuan Summers |work=NOLA.com |date=February 7, 2012 |access-date=September 22, 2015}} In September 2012, Summers signed with the [[Charlotte Hornets|Charlotte Bobcats]].{{cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=10984 |title=Bobcats add Jeff Adrien, Paris Horne, Josh Owens, DaJuan Summers to training camp |work=HoopsHype.com |date=September 25, 2012 |access-date=September 22, 2015}} However, he was later waived by the Bobcats on October 27, 2012.{{cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=11319 |title=Bobcats waive Josh Owens and DaJuan Summers |work=HoopsHype.com |date=October 27, 2012 |access-date=September 22, 2015}} On December 3, 2012, Summers was acquired by the [[Maine Red Claws]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/maine/transactions_120312.html |title=RED CLAWS Futures All-Star roster for the 2013 NBA D-League All-Star Game.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/2013_nba_development_league_all_star_rosters_announced_2013_02_04.html |title=2013 NBA March 15, 2013, Summers signed a 10-day contract with the Los Angeles Clippers.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/dajuan-summers-signed-10-day-contract |title=DAJUAN SUMMERS SIGNED TO A |access-date=April 5, 2013}} On July 9, 2013, Summers was waived by the Clippers.{{cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=13685 |title=Clippers waive forward DaJuan Summers |work=InsideHoops.com |date=July 9, 2013 |access-date=July 9, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130910213353/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=13685 |archive-date=September 10, 2013 forward |url=http://www.euroleague.net/euroleaguenews/transactions/2013-14-signings/i/115171/8177 |work=Euroleague.net |date=July 31, 2013 |access-date=July 31, 2013}} He sent his family home from [[Kyiv]] due to [[2014 Ukrainian revolution|political unrest in Ukraine]], but stayed to finish the season.{{cite news |url=http://www.freep.com/article/20140713/SPORTS03/307130118/dajuan-summers |title=Former Piston DaJuan Summers had 'humbling' experience in Ukraine |last=Ellis |first=Vince |newspaper=[[Detroit Free Press]] |date=July 13, 2014 |access-date=July 13, 2014}} In July 2014, Summers joined the Brooklyn Nets for the [[2014 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-announce-summer-league-roster |title=Brooklyn Nets Announce Summer League Roster |work=NBA.com |date=July 1, 2014 |access-date=July 1, 2014}} On August 12, 2014, he signed with [[CB Gran Canaria|Gran Canaria]] of the [[Liga ACB]].{{cite web |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/131296/dajuan-summers-signs-with-gran-canaria.html |title=DaJuan Summers signs with Gran Canaria |work=Sportando.com |date=August 12, 2014 |access-date=September 22, 2015}} On September 22, 2015, Summers signed with the [[New York Knicks]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/knicks/knicks-sign-travis-trice-and-dajuan-summers |title=Knicks Sign Travis Trice and DaJuan Summers |work=NBA.com |date=September 22, 2015 |access-date=September 22, 2015}} However, he was later waived by the Knicks on October 23 after appearing in four preseason games.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/knicks/knicks-waive-five-players |title=Knicks Waive Five Players |work=NBA.com |date=October 23, 2015 |access-date=October 23, 2015}} On November 2, he was acquired by the [[Westchester Knicks]] as an affiliate player of New York.{{cite web |url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=5066025 |title=Westchester Knicks Finalize 2015–16 Training Camp Roster |work=OurSportsCentral.com |date=November 2, 2015 |access-date=November 3, 2015}} On November 23, he was named the D-League's Performer of the Week for games played Thursday, November 12, through Sunday, November 22. The honor marked the first of the 2015–16 season and the first in Westchester Knicks history.{{cite web |url=http://westchester.dleague.nba.com/news/dajuan-summers-wins-performer-of-the-week/ |title=DaJuan Summers Wins Performer of the Week |work=NBA.com |date=November 23, 2015 |access-date=November 23, 2015 |archive-date=November 24, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151124172042/http://westchester.dleague.nba.com/news/dajuan-summers-wins-performer-of-the-week/ |url-status=dead }} The following day, he was ruled out for the rest of the season with a left Achilles tendon injury, an injury he suffered on November 20 in the final two minutes of the team's win over the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]]{{cite web |url=http://westchester.dleague.nba.com/news/dajuan-summers-suffers-season-ending-injury/ |title=DaJuan Summers Suffers Season-Ending Injury |work=NBA.com |date=November 24, 2015 |access-date=November 24, 2015 |archive-date=November 25, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151125055944/http://westchester.dleague.nba.com/news/dajuan-summers-suffers-season-ending-injury/ |url-status=dead }} and was waived on November 24.{{cite web |url=http://basketball.realgm.com/dleague/teams/Westchester-Knicks/40/Transaction_History/2016/ |title=2015-2016 Westchester Knicks Transactions History |work=RealGM.com |access-date=January 16, 2016}} In three games, Summers led the Knicks to a 3–0 start and averaged 25.3 points, 10.3 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 2.0 steals per game. On July 28, 2016, Summers signed with Turkish club [[Karşıyaka Basket|Pınar Karşıyaka]] for the 2016–17 season.[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/207953/pinar-karsiyaka-agreed-to-terms-with-dajuan-summers.html Pinar Karsiyaka agreed to terms with DaJuan Summers] On August 3, 2017, he signed with Turkish club [[Galatasaray S.K. (men's basketball)|Galatasaray]] for the 2017–18 season.{{cite news|title=Galatasaray bolsters frontcourt with Summers|url=http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/83ntjbd98jvjn4qa|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170804060658/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/83ntjbd98jvjn4qa|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 4, 2017|access-date=August 3, 2017|work=Eurocupbasketball.com|date=August 3, 2017}} On July 12, 2019, he has signed with [[Levallois Metropolitans]] of the [[LNB Pro A]].{{Cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/dajuan-summers-signs-with-metropolitans-92/|title=DaJuan Summers signs with Metropolitans 92|date=July 12, 2019|publisher=Sportando|language=En|access-date=August 14, 2019}} Summers later joined [[Shimane Susanoo Magic]], averaging 17.4 points, 8.0 rebounds, 1.3 assists and 1.1 steals per game. On October 11, 2020, he signed with [[Indios de Mayagüez (basketball)|Indios de Mayagüez]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]] (BSN).{{cite web |last1=Modesti |first1=Luis |title=DaJuan Summers (ex Shimane SM) agreed terms with Mayaguez |url=https://www.latinbasket.com/Puerto-Rico/news/647854/DaJuan-Summers-(ex-Shimane-SM)-agreed-terms-with-Mayaguez |website=Eurobasket |access-date=October PBA Commissioner's Cup]].{{cite web|last=Dy|first=Richard|url=https://www.manilatimes.net/2023/09/16/sports/summers-perfect-for-rain-or-shine/1910297|title=Summers perfect for Rain or Shine|work=[[The
